ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The following figure shows the zonal distribution of vegetation in China. Read the figure and answer the following questions. <image1> The east-west width of forest vegetation in eastern China changes in the north-south direction; what is its dominant factor?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the zonal distribution of vegetation in China. The eastern forest vegetation area is located on the right side of the figure; in the north, north of the Qinling—Huaihe line, it is marked “deciduous broad-leaved forest,” and in the south, south of the Qinling—Huaihe line, it is marked “evergreen broad-leaved forest.” The widths of these two forest belts extending from east to west are not the same in the north-south direction. Then reason: This east-west width change is not determined by the names of the forest types themselves, but by how far humid water vapor can advance inland. The distribution of forests in eastern China is mainly controlled by oceanic water vapor brought by the summer monsoon. Monsoon water vapor decreases from the coast toward the inland, and the range of monsoon influence has north-south differences, thus causing the east-west width of eastern forest vegetation to change in the north-south direction. The dominant factor is the monsoon.
